title: Spent 1000 💎 on GameTorch and created a fire water Clippy as the tutorial character for my elemental monster fusion game.
author: MatthiasTh

comments.author: MatthiasTh
comments.body:
I actually stumbled across [GameTorch ](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1lmyx4c/what_im_working_on_this_weekend_perfect_animated/)here on Reddit while looking for an AI-based sprite sheet generator. I had this weirdly specific idea stuck in my head: I wanted to turn Clippy into a fire-and-water elemental and use him as the tutorial character for my elemental monster fusion game [Fusiomon](https://www.fusiomon.com/).

So I started by generating some base sprites using ChatGPT’s new image model (4o), then took the result and ran it through GameTorch with a simple "idle" or "looking around" prompt to get a usable sheet.

To be honest, it took *a lot* of trial and error.. and a fair amount of manual cleanup and post-processing in Photoshop.. but I'm genuinely happy with the result (at least as a temporary placeholder).

Huge thanks to u/gametorch for making this tool. It made a strange idea come to life.

replies.author: gametorch
replies.body: Omg thank you so much! Yes, I'm working really hard to make this better every day. I can't wait to say where the models end up 1 year from now!

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Honestly, it really depends not just on what it looks like, but *how* it's presented.

It might pass if the tutorial dialogue and overall tone of the game is especially self aware that it's a work of parody, but not if you just throw a paperclip up in there and keep the rest serious.

Unless the game is *specifically* a parody game from top to bottom, any IP attorney is likely going to caution them to take it out given how litigious Microsoft can be.  The argument alone likely isn't worth whatever value the joke is bringing to the table.
